guidance: Model estimate of the main geomagnetic field, not a survey. Steel nearby, local ore bodies and a compass's own deviation card are outside the model, and the model is replaced every five years: check a current chart or an authoritative declination service before navigating on the result.
method: Declination, also called magnetic variation, is the angle from true north to magnetic north, counted positive east: a value of 1.3 degrees east means a magnetic bearing plus 1.3 degrees is the true bearing. The page evaluates the World Magnetic Model 2025 (WMM2025), a degree-12 spherical-harmonic model whose Gauss coefficients are given at epoch 2025.0 with annual secular-variation terms. The potential is V = a * sum over n = 1..12 of (a/r)^(n+1) * sum over m = 0..n of (g(n,m) cos(m L) + h(n,m) sin(m L)) P(n,m)(cos theta), with a = 6,371.2 km, r the geocentric radius, theta the geocentric colatitude and P the Schmidt quasi-normalised associated Legendre functions, which this page evaluates fully normalised and compensates by dividing each coefficient by sqrt(2n+1). The field is B = -grad V, giving a radial component from (n+1)(a/r)^(n+2), a colatitude component from the theta derivative of P and an east component from m times the longitude terms, with (a/r)^(n+2) as the radial power at every degree. The geodetic position is converted to geocentric radius and colatitude with the WGS84 ellipsoid (a = 6,378.137 km, 1/f = 298.257223563), and the resulting spherical components are rotated back to the geodetic north, east and down axes with the cosine and sine of the difference between geodetic and geocentric latitude. Declination is atan2(east, north), inclination atan2(down, horizontal), horizontal intensity is the quadrature sum of north and east, and total intensity includes down. The date is converted to a decimal year as elapsed days over the 365 or 366 days of that year, and the annual change is the declination one decimal year later minus the declination at the entered date, which is exact for the model because its secular variation is linear. Twelve published rows of the WMM2025 test-value file, at 0 and 100 km height, latitudes 80 N, 0 and 80 S and epochs 2025.0 and 2027.5, are replayed by the shipped suite to their printed precision, and the published declination rate column matches the computed annual change within 0.01 degree per year. Latitude is accepted from 89.999 S to 89.999 N because declination is undefined at the poles, longitude from -360 to 360 degrees with values past 180 folded back, elevation from -500 to 850,000 metres, and dates from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2029, each with its own refusal. The model describes the main field only: crustal anomalies, steel structures and a compass deviation card are not included, and the elevation is read as height above the ellipsoid, where a sea-level height shifts declination by only a few hundredths of a degree.
